role: The integrated server: subclasses MinecraftServer with the client's world settings, the pause-and-save on menu, the difficulty from the client's game settings and the view distance from the render distance.
scope_reason: This is the server the oracle runs; the lockstep pins its tick and the native replay reproduces it. Nothing in world.conf switches any of it. Deferred: native never writes save files; Java writes every checkpoint (product decision, not a gap for the GPU or the golden chain) (triage 2026-09-25, out/plan/remaining-2026-09-25.md).

notes: play-reload2-s1 exercises the pause save and the reload path. The tick loop itself is proven by test_servertick.c; this class adds only the pause and view-distance branches over MinecraftServer.tick. Closed by lane/idxworld: the pause save's in-game effect (every world's unload marks, serverreplay_pause_save) and the view-distance sync (IntegratedServer.tick's func_152611_a when the client's render distance changes: serverreplay_set_view_distance since lane/harness2; before it only the join's tick-1 change ran) are ported; the constructor and the world load are the oracle's, which the snapshot holds. The disk half is n/a (lane/idxworld): every save this game makes is the oracle's (a checkpoint's save, session.sh's Save and Quit through Java: AGENTS.md 'Playing a full game'), and the native engine reads what it wrote (region.c for the overworld's region files, the snapshot's saved chunks for DIM-1 and DIM1, structures.json, villages.nbt, worldinfo.nbt, player_server.nbt); writing those files natively is the deferred product work of the 2026-09-25 triage (SPEC.md NEXT, '11 deferred save-writing'; out/plan/remaining-2026-09-25.md, 'Deferred, not noise'). Within a session nothing reads a save back: an unloaded chunk waits whole in the in-memory region store (sr_store_chunk) with what writeChunkToNBT keeps of it (the entities it saves, in section order; the pending ticks relative to the world time), and a reload restores exactly that (the persist-* and play-reload recordings). Within a session nothing reads a save back: an unloaded chunk waits whole in the in-memory region store (sr_store_chunk) with what writeChunkToNBT keeps of it (the entities it saves, in section order; the pending ticks relative to the world time), and a reload restores exactly that (the persist-* and play-reload recordings).
